tasks.title: roundNext(): pending review first, select, health check, attempt record, prompt file
tasks.description:
Implement `roundNext()` in a new src/commands/round.ts — the pick step of `/cairn-run`. Do NOT register a CLI command in src/index.ts; task 99 does that.

CONTEXT: /cairn-run is an interactive run agent that loops: `cairn round next` → launch a `cairn-task-agent` subagent with 'Read <promptFile> and follow it' → `cairn round settle <id>`. All deterministic logic lives in the CLI; the run agent never reads tasks.json. Available pieces: selectNextTask / loadCompletedIds / buildIterationPrompt (src/task-selector.ts), runHealthCheck (src/health-check.ts), readTasksFile (src/tasks-file.ts), captureGitSha (src/post-task-reviewer.ts), run state (src/run-state.ts: an iteration counter plus attempts with phase 'executing' | 'awaiting-review'), settle's exported review prompt writer (src/settle.ts, task 97), and buildSystemPrompt with `mode: 'subagent'` (src/commands/run.ts, task 100).

roundNext({ projectRoot, dataDir, config, agents }, deps) returns a JSON-serializable object:
1. If any attempt record is in phase 'awaiting-review', return that review first: `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }`, rewriting the prompt file if it is missing (reuse task 97's writer). Reviews must not be lost to a crash.
2. Read tasks.json (readTasksFile with repair/recovery) and call selectNextTask. If nothing is ready: `{ verdict: 'round-done', blocked: <count of blocked tasks>, next }` with next telling the driver to send a notification and stop.
3. Run the health check (config.healthCheck, projectRoot). A failure's output is prepended to the iteration prompt exactly as runRun does.
4. Attempt record: create it with beforeSha = HEAD ONLY if none exists; on a re-pick keep the original beforeSha so the review covers every attempt.
5. Increment `iteration` in run state (a short updateRunState call) and store it on the record; it feeds `cairn task start --iteration`.
6. Write the prompt file: the system prompt (buildSystemPrompt in subagent mode) followed by a horizontal-rule separator line and the iteration prompt (buildIterationPrompt; pass sensible values for maxIterations and totalRemaining, and test them), to `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'task_<id>_prompt.md')` — i.e. `.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md`.
7. Return `{ verdict: 'task', taskId, title, iteration, model, promptFile, next }`, where next says: launch the Agent tool with subagent_type 'cairn-task-agent', model <model>, prompt 'Read <promptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <id>`.

MODEL: extract runRun's model resolution (run.ts ~564: task.model ?? 'opus', using the specialist agent's model when task.agent is set and task.model is not) into an exported shared helper (e.g. `resolveTaskModel(task, agents)`), used by both runRun and roundNext.

GITIGNORE: the prompt file is covered by the `task_*_prompt.md` suffix that task 97 already added to TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES — REUSE it; do NOT add another pattern. Just confirm the existing init.test.ts assertion covers `.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md`.

LOCKING: do not hold the run-state lock during the health check.

TESTS (test/commands/round.test.ts; temp dirs; health check and git injected): awaiting-review record returned first; round-done with blocked count; a new record gets the HEAD sha; a re-pick keeps the original sha; iteration increments across calls; the prompt file contains the subagent-mode system prompt and the task title; a health check failure is included; resolveTaskModel cases.

CONTEXT: roundNext() exists in src/commands/round.ts (task 98); settleTask with verdicts, the review phase and typed errors exists in src/settle.ts (tasks 91-97). tasks.title: Subagent mode for buildSystemPrompt
tasks.description:
Add a subagent mode to buildSystemPrompt (src/commands/run.ts) for tasks executed by a `cairn-task-agent` subagent under `/cairn-run`. The headless `cairn run` prompt must stay byte-for-byte unchanged; the existing buildSystemPrompt tests in test/commands/run.test.ts stay green.

CONTEXT: under /cairn-run, `cairn round next` writes this prompt into a prompt file and the run agent launches a subagent with 'Read <promptFile> and follow it'. The differences from headless mode follow from how subagents work: a subagent inherits the interactive session's working directory, and it is a subagent of a run agent that should receive only a tiny report.

CHANGES: add optional `mode?: 'headless' | 'subagent'` (default 'headless') to SystemPromptInput. In subagent mode:

# Task #100: Subagent mode for buildSystemPrompt

## TDD
Added a new `describe('subagent mode', ...)` block inside the existing `describe('buildSystemPrompt', ...)`
in test/commands/run.test.ts first (10 new tests), ran `bun test test/commands/run.test.ts` and watched
4 of them fail against the unmodified implementation (mode was accepted but ignored), then implemented.

## src/commands/run.ts
- `SystemPromptInput` gains `mode?: 'headless' | 'subagent'` (default `'headless'`), documented inline
  with why the two differ (spawnClaude's per-task cwd vs. a subagent inheriting the interactive session's
  cwd; completion flag vs. `cairn round next` detecting round-done itself).
- `buildSystemPrompt` destructures `mode = 'headless'` and derives `isSubagent`.
- DIRECTORY section: in subagent mode `dirLabel` is now `path.join(projectRoot, taskDir)` (or
  `projectRoot` when `taskDir` is empty) instead of the relative label, plus an added line telling the
  agent to cd there or use absolute paths (`dirCdInstruction`, empty string in headless mode).
- YOUR WORKFLOW: steps are now built as a `workflowSteps` array. Step 6 (completion-flag creation) is
  only pushed when `!isSubagent`; the final git-commit step is renumbered to 6 in subagent mode, 7 in
  headless mode. Steps 1-5 (start, files, implement, test, complete) are byte-identical text in both modes.
- New REPORT section (`reportSection`), appended only in subagent mode, right after the workflow steps:
  the 5-line report contract (task id, outcome, commit sha, blocking info), notes-file detail, and the
  in-progress/blocked-note fallback instruction for a genuine external blocker.
- CRITICAL RULES: built as a `criticalRules` array. The "Mark the task complete ... BEFORE creating
  <completeFlag>" line is only pushed when `!isSubagent`. All other rules (tasks.json ban, notes
  thoroughness, concise responses) are unchanged and present in both modes.
- SUBAGENT STRATEGY and the "root CLAUDE.md ... do NOT re-read it" CONTEXT line are untouched and appear
  verbatim in both modes (per task spec: nested subagents work, and the CLAUDE.md line was separately
  verified true for subagents).
- The specialist section (`specialistSection`) is completely unaffected by `mode` — it is computed before
  and embedded exactly as before in both modes; the task's `agent` field never becomes the subagent type.
- Headless-mode output is unchanged byte-for-byte: verified `buildSystemPrompt(makeInput())` ===
  `buildSystemPrompt(makeInput({ mode: 'headless' }))`, and all 40+ pre-existing buildSystemPrompt tests
  (which don't pass `mode`) still pass unmodified.

## test/commands/run.test.ts
New `describe('subagent mode', ...)` nested inside `describe('buildSystemPrompt', ...)`:
- default (no mode) === explicit `mode: 'headless'`
- headless mode still has the completion-flag step + critical rule (regression guard)
- subagent mode omits `.cairn_complete`, the flag-creation step text, and the "BEFORE creating" rule
- subagent mode states the absolute working directory (both with and without taskDir) + cd/absolute-paths instruction
- subagent mode has the 5-line report contract (task id, commit sha, --notes-file, blocked)
- subagent mode keeps SUBAGENT STRATEGY and the CLAUDE.md do-not-re-read line
- subagent mode still embeds SPECIALIST INSTRUCTIONS when a specialist is assigned
- subagent mode keeps the tasks.json Edit/Write ban and `cairn task start`/`complete` instructions

- Nothing in `cairn round next` / `/cairn-run` wires `mode: 'subagent'` yet — this task only adds the

  test/commands/run.test.ts only). A future task presumably passes `mode: 'subagent'` when constructing
  the prompt file that `cairn round next` writes.

tasks.title: cairn hook pre-tool-use: agent_type-aware containment hook (fail-open, logged)
tasks.description:
Implement `cairn hook pre-tool-use`: a Claude Code PreToolUse hook (JSON on stdin) that mechanically contains subagents under /cairn-run.

CONTEXT: under /cairn-run, subagents follow the interactive session's permission mode (recommended: bypassPermissions), so per-agent --allowedTools scoping doesn't apply and agent frontmatter can't express path scopes. Probe results from a throwaway repo with interactive `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`:
- Main-session tool calls have NO `agent_id` and NO `agent_type` keys (absent, not null). Subagent calls carry `agent_id` plus `agent_type`: 'general-purpose' for the built-in, the agent's frontmatter `name` for custom agents (e.g. 'post-task-reviewer').
- An internal Claude Code helper also fires the hook: a Bash call (`printf 'wait for it'`) with an `agent_id` but NO `agent_type` key. A missing agent_type is normal, not an error.
- Input also includes hook_event_name, permission_mode (e.g. bypassPermissions), tool_name, tool_input, cwd, session_id, transcript_path, tool_use_id.
- Hook denies bind even under bypass mode. Exit 2 shows the agent `PreToolUse:Write hook error: [<script>]: <stderr>`; exit 0 with stdout JSON `{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: <reason> } }` shows only the reason. USE THE JSON FORM.
- Any other failure (exit 1, or a missing binary with exit 127) lets the call through SILENTLY.

DECISION FUNCTION (pure, exported; e.g. src/hook-policy.ts or inside src/commands/hook.ts): `decidePreToolUse(input, ctx)` returning `{ decision: 'allow' }` or `{ decision: 'deny', reason }`, where ctx holds the resolved tasksFilePath, reviewsDir and projectRoot.
- Fast path: no `agent_id` → allow immediately (main session, generate-tasks, and every headless `cairn run` agent — the hook is a no-op for them). tool_name not Edit/Write/Bash → allow.
- Rule 1: any subagent (agent_id present, agent_type or not) calling Edit or Write whose tool_input.file_path resolves (relative paths against input.cwd) to the tasks.json path → deny, with a reason pointing to the `cairn task` subcommands.
- Rule 2: only when agent_type === 'post-task-reviewer' exactly: Edit/Write allowed only for paths inside the resolved reviews dir; Bash allowed only when every subcommand (split on &&, ||, ;, |, & and newlines, as buildCommandRules in src/claude-settings.ts documents) starts with one of the prefixes derived from the exported GIT_INSPECTION_RULES (e.g. 'git diff') — derive them from that list, do not duplicate it. Anything else from the reviewer → deny with a reason.
- Everything else → allow (print nothing, exit 0).

CLI: register a `hook` command group with `pre-tool-use` in src/index.ts.
- FAST STARTUP: the hook fires on every Edit/Write/Bash call in every session in the project. index.ts's preAction runs setupProjectContext (loadConfig, discoverAgents, possibly `git rev-parse`) — skip that for the hook command (e.g. check the action command's name in the preAction hook). Resolve only what is needed, lazily, after the fast path: project root from input.cwd via findProjectRoot, data dir via findDataDir (never BRAND.dataDir directly), reviews dir = <dataDir>/reviews, tasks file = <dataDir>/tasks.json.
- FAIL OPEN, VISIBLY: on any internal error (unparseable stdin, data dir not found, malformed cairn.json, any unexpected exception) never print a deny and NEVER exit 2; exit 1 and append a timestamped error line to the hook-error log `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'hook_errors.log')` — i.e. `.cairn_hook_errors.log` — whenever a data dir can be found (swallow failures writing the log). A malformed cairn.json must be logged, not crash with a stack trace.
- Deny: exit 0 with the hookSpecificOutput JSON on stdout.

SURFACING: roundNext in src/commands/round.ts (task 98) adds a `warnings: string[]` entry when the hook-error log exists and is non-empty, e.g. 'Hook errors logged in <path> (<n> lines) — the /cairn-run containment hook may not be working'.

GITIGNORE (required): add `'hook_errors.log'` to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` in src/commands/init.ts and update the ignore-block assertions in test/commands/init.test.ts.

TESTS (test/commands/hook.test.ts, fixtures modeled on the real probe payloads): main-session Write to tasks.json → allow; general-purpose subagent Write to tasks.json → deny; a relative file_path resolving to tasks.json → deny; internal helper (agent_id, no agent_type) Bash printf → allow; post-task-reviewer Write inside reviews/ → allow, outside → deny; reviewer Bash `git diff abc..HEAD` → allow, `git commit -m x`, `bun test`, `git diff && rm x` → deny; CLI handler: garbage stdin → non-zero exit, no deny output, error appended to the log; deny output JSON shape. Also: test/commands/round.test.ts warning when the log is non-empty; test/index.test.ts registration.

tasks.title: /cairn-run slash command (commands/cairn-run.md)
tasks.description:
Write the `/cairn-run` slash command at `commands/cairn-run.md`. The repo-root commands/ directory is copied into projects' .claude/commands/ by installSlashCommands (src/commands/init.ts); do not hand-edit .claude/commands/.

CONTEXT: /cairn-run runs a full Cairn round from an interactive Claude Code session (reachable from a phone via Remote Control) instead of headless `cairn run`. The session is the RUN AGENT; all deterministic logic is in the CLI:
- `cairn round next` prints JSON: `{ verdict: 'task', taskId, title, iteration, model, promptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'round-done', blocked, next }`, optionally with `warnings`.
- `cairn round settle <id> [--reviewed]` prints a JSON verdict: `retry` (mode 'continue' | 'fresh', reason, failure tail), `review` (reviewPromptFile), `blocked` (reason), `done`, `already-settled`. Every verdict has a `next` hint. Exit 0 for all verdicts; non-zero means the command itself failed.
- Task agents: subagent_type `cairn-task-agent` (maxTurns 150), return at most 5 lines. Reviewer: subagent_type `post-task-reviewer`, returns one line (PASS or CONCERNS).
Read src/commands/round.ts and src/settle.ts to match the actual JSON fields before writing.

THE COMMAND FILE must instruct the run agent to:
1. Loop: run `cairn round next` and act on the verdict. For `task`: launch the Agent tool with subagent_type 'cairn-task-agent', the model from the JSON, and prompt 'Read <promptFile> and follow it'; remember the returned agent id; then run `cairn round settle <taskId>`.
2. On `review` (from next or settle): launch Agent with subagent_type 'post-task-reviewer' and prompt 'Read <reviewPromptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <taskId> --reviewed`.
3. On `retry` with mode 'continue': SendMessage to the same task agent id with the reason/failure, asking it to finish, then settle again. If the agent id is unknown (e.g. after compaction or resume), fall back to a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file. Mode 'fresh': launch a new cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then settle.
4. On `blocked`: send a PushNotification (task id + reason) and continue the loop — never pause with AskUserQuestion.
5. On `round-done`: send a PushNotification with a short summary, then stop.
6. On any non-zero exit from a `cairn round` command: send a PushNotification with the stderr line and STOP.
7. Surface `warnings` from next (e.g. hook errors) to the user once.
8. Rules: agents run one at a time, never in parallel and never nested (the task agent must not launch the reviewer); the run agent NEVER reads tasks.json, diffs or test logs itself and never edits tasks.json; always follow each command's `next` hint so a compacted, resumed or fresh session behaves the same; keep its own messages terse so a round of up to ~20 tasks fits without relying on compaction.
9. A permission-mode note (the command cannot set the mode): recommend launching the session in bypassPermissions — the PreToolUse hook seeded by `cairn init` (`cairn hook pre-tool-use`) still denies subagent edits to tasks.json and scopes the reviewer, and hook denies bind under bypass; `auto` mode can be tried, but its classifier may wrongly deny routine actions (git commit, bun test, cairn task); default/acceptEdits will stall an unattended round on permission prompts.
10. Frontmatter with a description, following the format of commands/generate-tasks.md and commands/review-tasks.md.

TESTS (test/commands/init.test.ts): installSlashCommands with a cairnRoot override pointing at this repo root and a temp project dir installs cairn-run.md; a content test asserts the file mentions `cairn round next`, `cairn round settle`, `--reviewed`, `cairn-task-agent`, `post-task-reviewer`, SendMessage, PushNotification and bypassPermissions.

TDD: write the failing test first, run it and watch it fail, then implement until it passes — all within this task.

TEMP DIRS ONLY: never run `cairn init` or the init/claude-settings functions against this repository's root; exercise them only in temp directories created by the tests (fs.mkdtempSync).

COMMIT: stage only the files you changed (never `git add -A` or `git add .`) — cairn.json has an uncommitted user change that must not be committed.

tasks.title: Migrate .cairn/instructions.md to CLAUDE.local.md (init migration, gitignore warning, deprecation, README)
tasks.description:
Migrate personal instructions from `.cairn/instructions.md` to Claude Code's native `CLAUDE.local.md` at the project root.

CONTEXT: loadPersonalInstructions (src/personal-instructions.ts) reads `<dataDir>/instructions.md` and is injected into four agents: execution (buildSystemPrompt, src/commands/run.ts), post-task reviewer (buildPostTaskReviewUserPrompt, src/post-task-reviewer.ts), plan (src/commands/plan.ts) and summarize (src/commands/summarize.ts). CLAUDE.local.md is loaded natively by every Claude Code session in the project — including headless `claude -p` agents (unless --bare) and Agent-tool subagents (verified for general-purpose) — so Cairn no longer needs to inject it. Note that it applies to ALL sessions in the project, not only Cairn's agents.

CHANGES:
1. Loader deprecation (one release): loadPersonalInstructions keeps reading instructions.md when present, but writes a once-per-process deprecation warning to stderr: instructions.md is deprecated; move it to CLAUDE.local.md (re-run `cairn init` to migrate). Do NOT delete the loader or its four call sites this round.
2. `cairn init` (src/commands/init.ts):
- If `<dataDir>/instructions.md` exists with non-blank content, prompt 'Move .cairn/instructions.md into CLAUDE.local.md? [Y/n]'. On yes: append its content to `<projectRoot>/CLAUDE.local.md` (create the file if absent; when appending to an existing file, separate with a blank line and a `## Personal instructions (migrated from .cairn/instructions.md)` heading), then delete instructions.md. Never overwrite existing CLAUDE.local.md content.
- Replace createInstructionsFile's offer to create instructions.md with an offer to create/open CLAUDE.local.md at the project root (keep the $EDITOR / injected spawnSync mechanism the tests use).
- Gitignore: WARN only — do NOT edit .gitignore or git config — when CLAUDE.local.md is not gitignored. Check with `git check-ignore -q CLAUDE.local.md` run from projectRoot (inject the runner for tests; outside a git repo, skip silently). Mirror the existing warning style installClaudeSettings uses for `.claude/settings.local.json` ('add ... to your .gitignore yourself'; Cairn does not edit .gitignore for you). Keep 'instructions.md' in the data-dir GITIGNORE_CONTENT for the deprecation release.
3. README.md: the 'Personal Agent Instructions' section (~line 198) and the other instructions.md mentions (~lines 85, 313-314, 352). Document CLAUDE.local.md as the mechanism; fix the wrong claims that instructions reach 'execution agents only (not planning)' / are 'only injected during cairn run' — the legacy file reached execution, reviewer, plan and summarize agents, and CLAUDE.local.md reaches every session, including Cairn's headless agents and /cairn-run subagents; note the deprecation and the init migration.

This repository has its own CLAUDE.local.md and .cairn/instructions.md — do not migrate, edit or delete them.

TESTS: test/personal-instructions.test.ts — deprecation warning emitted once, content still returned. test/commands/init.test.ts — migration yes/no; append with heading to an existing CLAUDE.local.md; instructions.md removed on yes and kept on no; gitignore warning shown when check-ignore reports not-ignored and absent when ignored. Init tests feed prompt answers POSITIONALLY — update every affected answer sequence for the changed/added prompts.

tasks.title: Docs: CLAUDE.md and README.md for /cairn-run, cairn round, run state, hook enforcement
tasks.description:
Update the repo-root CLAUDE.md and README.md for Round 15. Documentation only — do not change code.

Read the current code first (src/settle.ts, src/run-state.ts, src/commands/round.ts, src/commands/hook.ts, src/claude-settings.ts, src/commands/init.ts, src/post-task-reviewer.ts, agents/cairn-task-agent.md, agents/post-task-reviewer.md, commands/cairn-run.md) and document what was actually built, not what was planned.

COVER:
1. Two ways to run a round: headless `cairn run` (the existing loop, a fresh `claude -p` per task) and interactive `/cairn-run` (a session reachable via Remote Control that drives `cairn round next` / `cairn round settle <id> [--reviewed] [--before-sha] [--test-timeout]`, launching `cairn-task-agent` subagents and the post-task-reviewer subagent one after another, never nested). Both share settleTask (src/settle.ts). Add `cairn round` (and `cairn hook`) to CLAUDE.md's execution-flow/command list and README's Commands section; explain why round commands are not under `cairn task` (a task agent calling settle would archive and skip its own review).
2. Run state: gitignored `.cairn_run_state.json` holding the iteration counter and per-task attempt records (beforeSha, reverts, stalls, incompletes, phase); counters survive restarts and compaction; `cairn task set-status` resets a task's record; thresholds are fixed (reverts 2, stalls 3, incompletes 3); settle order is validate → archive → review gate; verdicts and exit codes (0 for every verdict). Test output goes to `.cairn_task_<id>_tests.log`; prompts to `.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md` and `.cairn_task_<id>_review_prompt.md`. Update CLAUDE.md's per-project data layout and the Conventions line saying where logic lives. Remove any surviving claim that guard counters are in-memory/per-run.
3. Enforcement under /cairn-run, added to CLAUDE.md's Agent workflow section WITHOUT weakening or contradicting the existing headless story (execution agents under `cairn run` are bound only by their system prompt; reviewer/planner by --allowedTools; headless mode is deny-by-default). Subagents follow the interactive session's permission mode, so --allowedTools scoping doesn't carry over. The PreToolUse hook `cairn hook pre-tool-use`, seeded into .claude/settings.local.json by init, checks agent_id/agent_type: it denies any subagent Edit/Write to tasks.json and scopes post-task-reviewer to reviews/ writes and read-only git Bash; it denies via exit 0 + JSON permissionDecision; it is FAIL-OPEN (internal errors exit non-zero, are logged to `.cairn_hook_errors.log`, and are surfaced by `cairn round next`); it is a no-op for main sessions, generate-tasks and headless `cairn run` agents (no agent_id). Record the hook probe facts so they are never re-derived: hook denies bind under bypassPermissions; exit 1 / 127 lets calls through silently; internal helpers send agent_id without agent_type.
4. Recommended permission mode for /cairn-run: bypassPermissions + hook; auto may be tried; default/acceptEdits stall unattended rounds.
5. The reviewer no longer runs tests (settle validates first; it gets a summary plus the log path), has an explicit tools list, and its headless grant no longer includes test-command rules — update CLAUDE.md's sentence saying the reviewer's Bash grants include 'one prefix rule per subcommand of the task's declared tests entries'.
6. CLAUDE.local.md replaces .cairn/instructions.md (deprecated for one release) — make CLAUDE.md consistent with README where task 106 left gaps.
7. Do NOT remove or alter the 'Pin/unpin procedure for self-modifying rounds' section.

PINNED BINARY (self-modifying round): do NOT modify cairn.json's healthCheck value and do NOT run ./install.sh. The user has pinned ~/.local/bin/cairn to a known-good build and redirected the health check to a throwaway outfile (/tmp/cairn-healthcheck).

COMMIT: stage only CLAUDE.md and README.md (never `git add -A` or `git add .`) — cairn.json has an uncommitted user change that must not be committed.
